The Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) section aims to uncover patterns, relationships, and insights within the dataset to guide the next stages of the project. The primary goal of this analysis is to better understand the distribution of key health indicators, such as `BMI`, `diabetes prevalence`, and `hypertension control`, and their association with health risk categories (`Low`, `Moderate`, `High Risk`). By analyzing these variables across dimensions like gender and health status, we can identify critical trends and disparities that drive chronic disease risks.

The motivation behind this EDA is to validate assumptions, detect data anomalies, and reveal meaningful relationships between features that will inform model building. For instance, determining how BMI and diabetes prevalence are correlated can guide feature engineering, while exploring categorical associations, such as gender and health risk, can uncover hidden patterns critical to supervised learning tasks. The insights gained here will serve as a foundation for feature selection, data transformations, and model optimization in subsequent steps.
